Fannon on Instagram\u003C/a>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>\u003Cspan style=\"font-size:22px;\">\u003Cstrong>Awards\u003C/strong>\u003C/span>\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cem>2017 MAC Coach of the Year \u003Cbr />\r\n2018 MAC Coach of the Year\u003Cbr />\r\n2019 MAC Coach of the Year\u003C/em>\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Entering his seventh season in 2026, Matt Fannon has continued to build in Ames. After being hired on Dec. 17 of 2019, the Cyclones have shown progress under Fannon's guidance. The Cyclones finished the 2021 season with the most wins since 2016 and ended the season by taking #8 TCU to PK's. In 2022, Iowa State recorded its first win over a ranked opponent since 2016 and its first victory over in-state rival Iowa since 2018. ISU's momentum continued into 2023 as Fannon's squad earned its most conference wins since 2007.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2025, Coach Fannon led Iowa State to its best start to a season since 2013, as ISU opened the year undefeated through three games. Fannon also oversaw a three-game win streak as ISU downed UND, UNI and Arizona in consecutive weeks marking the first three-game win streak since 2016. Fannon helped captain the Cyclones to the program’s 200\u003Csup>th\u003C/sup> win at Creighton on 8/21.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2024, the Cyclones were hampered by injuries, losing four starters. Fannon helped guide the Cyclones to be competitive in most every game, but couldn't get over the hump as the team recorded a single season school record six ties. The team had four draws in conference play which was also the most in a single season in Iowa State history.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Iowa State's 2023 season featured the first of an expanded Big 12 as the Cyclones finished the season strong, beating two of their final three opponents. ISU finished with six wins, the most under Coach Fannon and the program's most since 2016. The team also scored 19 goals which is the most since the 2014 team converted 21 scores.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The 2022 season also marked the first season in Ames that Fannon was able to recruit the incoming freshman and transfer class in-person and play a full schedule. Fannon’s 2022 squad dropped just ten games, which, other than the COVID-shortened season, was the fewest since 2016.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2020, the Cyclones battled perhaps the toughest schedule the Cyclones had ever faced. Iowa State played four opponents ranked in the top 15 nationally by the United Soccer Coaches poll - the most in program history. The team ending the 2020-21 season on a five-match unbeaten streak - the program’s longest since 2010. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Prior to Iowa State, Fannon was the three-time reigning Mid-American Conference Coach of the Year when he was named the sixth Head Women’s Soccer Coach in Iowa State history.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Fannon guided Bowling Green State to a 41-18-7 mark (26-6-1 in the MAC) in his three seasons there, winning league Coach-of-the-Year honors each season. He won more games at BGSU than the school won in the eight prior years combined. In his rookie season, the Falcons won 13 games, the second-most in school history. He tied the university’s season win mark (14) his final two years.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Bowling Green won both the MAC regular-season and tournament championships in 2018 and 2019. The Falcons advanced to the NCAA Championship in both of those campaigns.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Fannon’s teams have adopted an aggressive, attacking style throughout his career which leads to many scoring opportunities as well as limiting scoring chances for the opponent.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The 2017 team scored 43 goals, and the 2019 team scored 46 to rank as the two highest-scoring seasons in school history. The 2018 squad had the second-best defensive scoring average in Bowling Green annals.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2018, BGSU dropped an early season match to 15\u003Csup>th\u003C/sup>-ranked Northwestern and then went on to play the next 1,008 minutes (nearly 17 hours of match time) without trailing. Fannon’s 2018 team led the MAC in goals scored as well as fewest goals allowed.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>The 2019 Falcons again led the conference in scoring offense and defense. BGSU was the only school to average more than two goals per league game (2.545) and was one of two schools to allow fewer than a goal per game (0.73). Falcon student-athletes took home MAC Offensive Player of the Year honors in 2017, 2018 and 2019, as well as MAC Defensive Player of the Year recognition in 2018 and 2019.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Off the pitch, BGSU had record numbers of MAC academic honorees and had four MAC Distinguished Scholar-Athletes in his first two seasons at the helm. BGSU also had one CoSIDA Academic All-American, a Senior CLASS All-American and maintained a team GPA above 3.5 during his tenure.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Fannon, a native of York, England, has made a rapid climb on the college coaching ladder. He was an assistant at Regis University and the University of Wyoming before assuming the head coaching responsibilities at Wittenberg (2013-16) and Bowling Green State (2017-19).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In his four seasons as head coach, the Tigers were 40-26-10. Wittenberg made the NCAA Division III Tournament his final year. He was named NCAC Coach of the Year that season.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Fannon has his NSCAA Premier diploma and earned his Football Association Coaching Certificate in England. He also has a United States Soccer Federation Goalkeeping License.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Fannon earned his B.S. degree in physical education from Davis and Elkins College (2008) and added a Master’s degree in Soccer Coaching Education from Ohio University (2015).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>He was a two-time first-team all-region and first-team all-conference player for the Senators. Fannon also played a year at Dutchess Community College before attending Davis and Elkins.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Fannon and his wife, Julie, have two daughters: Rowen and Parker was hired as an Assistant Soccer Coach at Iowa State on August 9, 2024, and held the position until February of 2026.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Parker has 26 years of head coaching experience on his resume and comes to Ames after a 24-year stint as the head coach of the Stevens Institute of Technology soccer program. Overall, he has 28 years of collegiate coaching experience across NCAA Division I and Division III programs. Besides Stevens, Parker also coached at Georgetown as an assistant (1995-98) and Saint Peter's as head coach (1998-99).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In 2025, Parker helped the production of freshman Megan Walters, who scored three goals on the year – the most by an ISU freshman since 2016. Parker also helped ISU to its best three-game start in the last 12 years.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>In his first season in Ames, Parker helped Iowa State finish 3-9-6, setting a new school record for draws in a season.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>At Stevens, Parker oversaw a program that made 22 consecutive postseason appearances. He also earned 16 conference championship titles during his time as a head coach, making the NCAA postseason 13 times. As part of those NCAA postseason runs, Parker helped lead Stevens to three Sweet 16 appearances. In total, Parker led Stevens to 302 victories - a program record.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>As a head coach, Parker has over 500 games under his belt. Four of his previous assistants have gone on to become head coaches of their own at the college ranks. Under his guidance, Parker had nine Academic All-Americans, and four athletes earned All-American honors for their performance on the pitch.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>He holds certifications from the United States Soccer Federation and NSCAA/United Soccer Coaches Association and has completed courses from the United European Football Association, the Czech Football Association, and the Football Association of Ireland. Parker served four years on the NCAA Division III Women's Soccer Committee, including two as national chair.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Parker graduated from Texas Tech in 1991 with a Bachelor of Arts in broadcast journalism and then earned his Master of Arts from TTU in sports administration in Having started zero games prior, Cannistraro collected three clean sheets, an assist and 64 saves.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Junion arrived in Ames after spending three years (2022-24) at Western Kentucky where he was on the soccer staff as an Assistant Coach. During his time in Bowling Green, Goalkeeper Maddie Davis moved to third all-time in program history for clean sheets in a career. Davis also amassed three C-USA Goalkeeper of the Week awards, made the All-C-USA Second Team and was the C-USA Goalkeeper of the Year in 2024. Another standout under Junion, GK Alexis Bach, amassed one C-USA Goalkeeper of the Week honor and was All-CUSA Second Team in 2022. The Hilltoppers boasted less than 1 GAA in C-USA play during his tenure.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>At WKU, Junion was also responsible for managing the recruiting database, team and player analysis, small group and individual sessions, facilitating leadership curriculum sessions, digital design, and directing youth camps. He was also involved in the local club scene as a Director of Goalkeeping and Head Coach of the u19 age group.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Junion spent the 2021 season at Bellarmine University as an assistant. He primarily focused on the development of goalkeepers in his role with the Knights. Towards the end of his time with Bellarmine, Junion's role expanded to include additional recruiting, player campus visits and team training responsibilities. Junion's lone season with the Knights was only the second year of competing in Division I for Bellarmine. The team made its first conference semifinal appearance after two penalty kicks were saved against the No. 1 seed in the quarterfinals. The Knights secured five team clean sheets that season. During that time, he was also involved as a u19 coach at Racing Louisville.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Junion's playing career concluded in a reserve role at Xavier University (2015-16) after injuries.
